text: Resubmitting closes the Resolution Center line of communication, so the safe order is: reply with evidence (e.g. screen recording), wait for the reviewer to confirm or answer, then resubmit only if a code or metadata change is needed. Replies without resubmitting do get answers in practice, but replying alone does not necessarily trigger a fresh review cycle. (medium confidence)

Apple's help text does not document file-size limits, accepted video formats, or whether a link versus an uploaded file is preferred for screen recordings; the pages checked state only that other file types are allowed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Apple's Resolution Center reply lets Account Holder, Admin, or App Manager roles send up to 4,000 characters and attach files (screenshots, supporting documents) to a rejection reply; the thread stays open only until the developer resubmits to App Review. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)
A metadata-rejected submission can be fixed by editing the cited metadata and resubmitting the same build; a binary rejection requires uploading and selecting a new build. (high confidence)

For features hard to reproduce in review (hardware, special environments, unusual behaviour), Apple expects a demo video or the hardware; a video can be attached via the Attachment field in App Review Information, with explanations or links in Review Notes. (high confidence)

Apple's FAQ says screenshots may be attached to the Resolution Center reply to show how the app addresses the rejection, and that the Notes/attachments in App Review Information can explain where reviewers find specific features; this applies to a menu-bar app with no main window. (medium confidence)

Appeals go to the App Review Board through App Store Connect: give specific reasons the app complies, submit one appeal per rejected submission, and answer any pending information request before appealing. (high confidence)

Apple generally responds to Resolution Center messages within about 24 hours, but forum reports describe repetitive copy-paste replies that ignore the developer's specific question. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)
